Help

        

          
          

            

            

              
Open file accepts a Midihub preset (.mhp), a device setup (.mhd), or Piper JSON. Downloads save a new file and leave your original intact.

              
    
                
  • Download Preset saves the selected preset as .mhp. If it uses a custom tuning, that tuning must be available on the receiving device.
    • 
                
  • Download Everything saves all eight presets, device settings, and tuning tables from an open setup.
    • 
                
  • Download JSON saves the open document with instructions for an AI agent. Give the file to your agent with the changes you want, then open the returned JSON in Piper to try it.
    • 
              

            

          

          

            

            

              
New preset starts a standalone preset or clears a slot you choose in an open setup. New setup creates eight slots. Use Device settings to edit shared port names and tunings.

              
To copy a preset between files, open the destination setup first. In Presets → Copy preset, choose Another file, select the source and destination slots, then choose Replace preset. Undo restores the previous contents.

            

          

          

            

            

              
Drag a pipe from Pipes onto a pipeline. To start a new pipeline, drop an input on empty map space. Click a pipe to edit its parameters or MIDI mappings.

              
In Virtual routing, select a pipeline number to jump to the pipe connected to that virtual port. To use the map’s displayed pipeline order in your preset, choose Presets → Apply pipeline order.

              
Press Delete to remove the selected pipe. On a pipeline’s starting input, this removes the whole pipeline. Undo restores it.

            

          

          

            

            

              
Choose the input tab that feeds your pipeline, then Add source. A Notes source plays a chord or an arpeggio. Turn on Hold to sustain the chord or repeat the arpeggio until you stop. Start input plays one input’s configured sources and Start all plays across inputs.

              
To try a controller mapping, add an Expression pedal, match its channel and CC to the mapping, and move the floating slider. Use MIDI message to send a single event.

              
If a note keeps sounding after you stop playback, use MIDI Panic to silence Piper and its selected hardware outputs.

              
Built-in instruments use WebAudioTinySynth under Apache 2.0.

            

          

          

            

            

              
To play from a controller, add a MIDI input source in MIDI Studio, allow MIDI access in your browser, and choose your device.

              
To hear the result on a synth, select its port under Destination for notes or a hardware input, or MIDI out for messages and pedals. If the ports aren’t listed yet, choose Find MIDI outputs…. The synth receives events that reach an output in your preset.

            

          

          

            

            

              
Open MIDI activity to see which messages entered a pipeline, reached an output, or were dropped. For one pipe’s messages, click it on the map and open Pipe activity.

              
Log messages filters the event list and its clipboard copy. Animated selects which events light up connections on the map. Enable clock ticks in either filter when you want to trace timing.

            

          

          

            

            

              
Drag empty map space to pan. Scroll to zoom at the pointer. Drag a panel’s dotted grip to dock it in a corner or reorder it. Double-click its width grip to restore its default width.

              
With the dotted grip focused, use Left or Right to change sides, Shift+Up or Shift+Down to change corners vertically, and Up or Down to reorder. Home restores the original position.
